newsitem.title: GERMANY: German TV says visa crime ring at Tehran embassy.
newsitem.headline: German TV says visa crime ring at Tehran embassy.

text.p: A German television station reported on Thursday that Iranians working at Bonn's embassy in Tehran stole about 20,000 visas over several years and sold them to foreigners seeking entry into Germany.

NDR television in Hamburg said the stolen visas went to an Iranian-German-Dutch smuggling ring that police estimate earned about 10 million marks ($6.4 million) organising illegal entries into Germany.

An international search warrant has been issued for the Iranian mastermind of the smuggling ring and one of his main aides, also an Iranian, has been detained in investigative custody in Hamburg since August, NDR said.
The foreign ministry in Bonn declined to comment on the report.

NDR said the ring often arranged faked invitations for businessmen or arranged to have visa requests denied without reason so they could sell applicants a fake visa later. The going rate for a fake visa was 3,000 marks. ($1=1.5608 Mark)
